lessons.title: Preparing kernel for dispatch
lessons.html:
The dispatch function

Dispatch is the last step before macadamia kernel leaves the factory for a buyer, a packer or an export port. At this point the product has its full value. A mistake at dispatch, such as the wrong grade on a pallet, damaged cartons or missing paperwork, can cost the business a whole consignment. As a dispatch supervisor or senior operator you make sure that the right product, in the right condition, with the right documents, goes to the right customer.

Working from the order

Every dispatch starts with an order or dispatch instruction. Check it for:

  • Customer name and delivery address or port.
  • Kernel style (for example wholes, halves, pieces) and grade.
  • Quantity: number of cartons or vacuum packs, and net mass.
  • Packaging, labelling and pallet requirements of the customer.
  • Collection date, transporter and any container or seal numbers.

Picking and checking the stock

  1. Pick stock from the store by lot or batch number, usually first expired, first out.
  2. Check that each carton label shows the correct product, grade, lot number, net mass and dates.
  3. Inspect packaging. Vacuum packs must be tight. Reject soft, punctured or damaged packs and cartons and report them.
  4. Check that quality control has released the lots. Never dispatch stock on hold.
  5. Build pallets to the customer's pattern and height, with corner boards and strapping or wrap as specified.
  6. Label each pallet with its pallet number and contents.

Protecting the product

Kernel is a food product with high oil content. It can pick up odours and go rancid if kept warm or exposed to moisture. Keep dispatch areas clean, cool and dry, free of pests and away from chemicals, fuel and strong smells. Follow the factory's food safety and hygiene rules, including hand washing and protective clothing.

lessons.title: Loading, documents and records
lessons.html:
Inspecting the vehicle or container

Before loading, inspect the truck or container. It must be:

  • Clean, dry and free of odours, pests, nails and broken floor boards.
  • Watertight, with doors and seals that work.
  • At the right temperature if a refrigerated unit is used, with the setting as instructed.

Record the inspection. If the vehicle fails, do not load it. Tell the transporter and your manager.

Loading safely

  • Only trained, authorised operators drive forklifts or pallet jacks.
  • Chock the truck wheels and make sure the vehicle cannot move before a forklift enters.
  • Keep people out of the loading zone while the forklift works.
  • Load to the plan so weight is spread evenly and pallets cannot shift. Use load straps or airbags where specified.
  • Count every pallet as it goes on and tick it off the dispatch list.

Documents

Depending on the customer and destination, the paperwork may include:

DocumentPurpose
Delivery note / dispatch noteLists what was sent; signed by the driver
Packing listPallets, cartons, lots and masses
Certificate of analysisQuality results for each lot from the lab
Export documentsPrepared with the export agent for shipments overseas

Record container and seal numbers. Seal the container in front of a witness where required and photograph the seal.

After dispatch

  • Update stock records so the system shows the stock has left.
  • File signed documents and send copies to the office and the customer as required.
  • Report any shortage, damage or delay at once.

Key points

  • Check the order: product, grade, quantity, packaging and customer requirements.
  • Dispatch only lots released by quality control, picked by batch number.
  • Inspect the vehicle; do not load a dirty, wet or smelly vehicle.
  • Load safely to plan and count every pallet.
  • Complete and file documents, seal numbers and stock updates.

quiz.question: What should you do with lots that quality control has placed on hold?

options.text: Never dispatch them until they are released
Relabel them with a new lot number

quiz.question: Why must kernel be kept away from fuel and strong smells?

options.text: Kernel has high oil content and can pick up odours
It is only a rule for export

quiz.question: What should you do if the truck arriving for loading is wet inside and smells?

options.text: Load it quickly before it rains
Do not load it; tell the transporter and your manager
Put plastic on the floor and load

quiz.question: Which document gives the quality results for each lot?
What must happen before a forklift enters a truck to load it?

options.text: The driver must start the engine
The wheels must be chocked so the truck cannot move
The stock records must be updated

quiz.question: Soft or punctured vacuum packs should be rejected and reported, not dispatched.
Stock records only need updating at the end of the season, not after each dispatch.
Which details should you check on the order before dispatch? (select all that apply)

options.text: The weather forecast for next month
